title: SolarEdge Confirms U.S. Inverter Offering Clear FCC Covered List
body_markdown:
*SolarEdge inverters remain available for new U.S. projects with no added approvals; U.S. manufacturing capacity and an independent SOC 2 Type II examination support America’s energy security*


**MILPITAS, Calif. – 11/17/26 –** SolarEdge Technologies, Inc. today confirmed that all of its inverters sold in the United States either hold FCC equipment authorizations or fall outside the scope of the Federal Communications Commission’s Covered List entry for foreign-produced power inverters, as revised by Public Notice DA 26-870. Customers can presently continue to specify, purchase and install SolarEdge inverters with no new approvals and no change to project timelines.


On July 28, the FCC added foreign-produced connected power inverters to its Covered List, citing the risk that remote connectivity could introduce vulnerabilities into U.S. energy infrastructure. Covered products can no longer receive FCC equipment authorizations required to import, market or sell them in the United States. On August 20, the FCC excluded inverters eligible for the Section 45X Advanced Manufacturing Production Credit, which include SolarEdge’s U.S.-manufactured residential and commercial inverters.


SolarEdge welcomes the FCC’s notice, which provides additional certainty for customers investing in solar technologies at a time when growing electricity demand and domestic manufacturing are increasing the importance of a secure and reliable grid. Project developers and installers with concerns about their current inverter selection, including exposure to foreign entity of concern (FEOC) restrictions, are encouraged to contact SolarEdge to learn how its solutions can help them move forward with confidence and regulatory alignment.


*“We look forward to continuing to work with industry stakeholders and policymakers to build on the success of policies such as the Section 45X Advanced Manufacturing Production Credit, driving continued investment in U.S. manufacturing and creating high-quality American jobs,”* said Gokul Krishnan, SVP and General Manager, North America, at SolarEdge. SolarEdge manufactures inverters for the U.S. market at two major production sites in Florida, Texas, supporting over 2,500 manufacturing jobs. and giving it the capacity to meet growing demand across residential, commercial, community. As new foreign-produced inverter models face restrictions, installers and developers can rely on SolarEdge, the commercial market leader*, for supply continuity.


SolarEdge has set cybersecurity as a key organizational priority, and its products are designed to comply with the technical requirements of leading frameworks, including ISO/IEC 27001 and the EU NIS2 Directive. SolarEdge has now completed an independent SOC 2 Type II examination of its cloud-based monitoring platform, covering the Security criteria. The examination holds particular significance as solar and energy storage supports critical energy infrastructure in the U.S.


Together, U.S. manufacturing capacity and robust cybersecurity position SolarEdge to deliver on national priorities for energy security, economic growth and American energy dominance.
